executor

ig-ZEK-yuh-tur -- Latin ex- ('out') plus sequi ('to follow'): the one who follows a plan all the way out. · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Executor is a person who carries something out and makes it happen.

A good idea is worthless without an executor willing to do the unglamorous work.

Worked Example

Someone sketches a brilliant plan for a school garden on a napkin; another person orders the soil, books the truck, recruits twelve volunteers, and has the beds planted by April.

The person who takes a plan off the page and makes it actually happen is the executor. Unlike the planner, who supplies the vision, the executor supplies the follow-through.

Your Turn

Answer correctly to continue.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

agent: An agent is one who acts to bring something about, often on someone else's behalf -- a travel agent books the trip you chose. An executor owns the whole follow-through: taking a particular plan and driving it to completion. An agent acts for you; an executor delivers the finished thing.

organizer: An organizer lines things up -- schedules, supplies, volunteers -- so that a plan is ready to run. An executor goes past arranging: the executor carries the plan through until the result actually exists. Organizing gets every piece in place; an executor makes the thing happen.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

planner: one who designs but does not carry out

bystander: someone present who takes no part

Where it sits · how official and broad the responsibility is — doer → executor → administrator

doer vs. executor: Doer is the plain, informal version of executor -- any hard worker can be called a doer, while an executor is specifically the person responsible for carrying out a particular plan.

administrator vs. executor: Administrator is more official than executor: an executor makes one plan or task happen, while an administrator runs the whole ongoing operation, budgets and staff included.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: out, fully (Latin)

Root — ecut

Root — ecut: to follow (from Latin sequi; in exsequi, 'to follow out to the end', the s of sequi merges into the x of ex-, leaving -ecut-)

Suffix — -or

Suffix — -or: one who does the action (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- ('out, fully') + ecut ('to follow', from Latin sequi -- its s merges into the x of ex-) + -or ('one who') spell executor: the one who follows a plan all the way out to the end, from the same root sequi that gives us sequence and consequence.

Use the root in a new word: sequence

Use the root in a new word: sequence: The dancers repeated the same sequence of steps until it looked effortless.

Word Choice

This unit teaches executor in its general sense: the one who makes something happen. Be aware that in law the word has a narrower use -- the executor of a will is the person appointed to carry out its instructions -- which is the same idea of 'carrying out,' applied to a document.
